items.title: Tepid Chelsea beaten by Sunderland who move off bottom
items.excerpt: Chelsea put in a tepid performance as Sunderland lifted themselves off the bottom of the Premier League table with a 1-0 win that eases the pressure on under-fire manager Regis Le Bris.
body: Chelsea put in a tepid performance as Sunderland lifted themselves off the bottom of the Premier League table with a 1-0 win that eases the pressure on under-fire manager Regis Le Bris.

Xabi Alonso's side were second-best throughout. None of their midfield attack won a duel or a tackle in the opening 20 minutes, while Sunderland's fight was best shown through Brian Brobbey's efforts up front.
The Dutch international smashed his way through Chelsea centre-backs Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill in a brutal first half - coming close to scoring twice, before eventually getting his rewards.

Ten minutes before half-time, he rolled past Colwill with immense strength to win a penalty, which Enzo Le Fee converted. Colwill was then taken off at half-time. items.title: Bournemouth win at Ipswich to record eight straight victories
items.excerpt: Bournemouth made it eight wins in a row in all competitions as they continued their charge up the Premier League table with a 2-1 win at Ipswich.
body: Bournemouth made it eight wins in a row in all competitions as they continued their charge up the Premier League table with a 2-1 win at Ipswich.
Evanilson scored for the fifth Premier League game running when taking advantage of a shocking error from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton, who tried to dribble around the striker.

Bournemouth arrived in Suffolk eager to complete an almost perfect month since the last international break with another three points and Alex Scott returned to the bench in another boost for Marco Rose.
Ipswich started the second half in nightmare fashion in a very sloppy overall performance, with the Cherries given a helping hand to score again after 27 seconds.

items.title: Sage in big trouble as Palace hit rock-bottom after defeat to Liverpool
items.excerpt: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park to inflict a fourth consecutive Premier League defeat on the hosts and leave Pierre Sage in a perilous position with his side bottom of the table.
body: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park to inflict a fourth consecutive Premier League defeat on the hosts and leave Pierre Sage in a perilous position with his side bottom of the table.

Eddie Nketiah pulled a goal back from the spot for Palace with the last kick of the game, but the damage was already done after Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz struck for Liverpool either side of half time before Alexander Isak added a third late on.

Liverpool secured a much-needed result following back-to-back defeats at Arsenal and Fenerbahce. items.title: Rangers end winless away run with comfortable victory at St Mirren
items.excerpt: Rangers moved one point behind Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic thanks to goals from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil in a 2-0 win over St Mirren.
body: Rangers moved one point behind Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic thanks to goals from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil in a 2-0 win over St Mirren.

Draws against Dundee and Hearts in their last two Premiership games away from Ibrox had blemished the Gers' focused title challenge, but Derek McInnes's side were determined to leave The Marbill Coaches Stadium without a mark on them.
In-form striker Ryan Naderi scored a penalty after 18 minutes after James Penrice was fouled - a decision Sky Sports' co-commentator James McFadden called "softer than soft".
Dan Neil added a second just after the hour mark with a deflected strike to extend the Light Blues' unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 games.

items.title: 'A different Noni?' Madueke finding a new level for Arsenal
items.excerpt: Noni Madueke lay sprawled on the turf, head in his hands, following his one-on-one miss late in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Hull . His frustration continued to show even after the final whistle.
body: Noni Madueke lay sprawled on the turf, head in his hands, following his one-on-one miss late in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Hull . His frustration continued to show even after the final whistle.

The winger's reaction showed the standards this "different Noni", to quote Mikel Arteta, is setting himself as he strives to reach another level. Bukayo Saka's injury was a significant setback to Arsenal. Madueke has made it his mission to soften the blow.

So far, he has filled in impressively. Arteta understood his demeanour after the game. "He knew he had three clear chances to score," he said, always demanding more. But there was also an acknowledgement of his crucial role in Martin Odegaard's goal.

Madueke's shot forced the Konstantinos Tzolakis save from which his captain scored. It was just one of many dangerous moments. His total of 13 touches in the opposition box was the most by an Arsenal in any Premier League game this season. items.title: Hits and misses: Could Konsa hold off Saliba's return?
items.excerpt: Arsenal did not produce a vintage attacking display against Hull but defensively there were few faults. Their seventh clean sheet in 10 Premier League games, and 10th in 16 overall, owed a lot to their centre-backs. Gabriel and Ezri Konsa e…
body: Arsenal did not produce a vintage attacking display against Hull but defensively there were few faults. Their seventh clean sheet in 10 Premier League games, and 10th in 16 overall, owed a lot to their centre-backs. Gabriel and Ezri Konsa excelled again.

William Saliba's impending return will put pressure on Konsa to retain his place but on current form he may keep hold of the shirt. Highlights from his display included a last-ditch block on Mohamed Ali-Cho when was suddenly exposed on the break. Arsenal 1-0 Hull - Match report and highlights As it happened | Teams | Stats

There was no self-congratulation afterwards. Instead he berated the referee for a perceived Hull foul, then got on with business. By the end of the game, he had won all seven of his duels and completed all but two of his 53 passes, a picture of composure.

He continues to make an immense contribution since his arrival at the club. Arsenal had one early scare when Elliot Stroud forced a save from David Raya but it is now 444 minutes without conceding a goal in the Premier League for the Gunners.

items.title: Forest end goal drought to make it three defeats in a row for Man City
items.excerpt: Liam Delap scored two as Nottingham Forest ended their goal drought in style to beat Manchester City 3-1 at the City Ground.
body: Liam Delap scored two as Nottingham Forest ended their goal drought in style to beat Manchester City 3-1 at the City Ground.

City had suffered back-to-back Premier League defeats but few could have expected Oliver Glasner's side to expose them this emphatically given that Forest were goalless let alone winless at home this season. Instead, their intensity was too much for City.

Forest fans had to wait almost six months and watch eight-and-a-half hours of football here without seeing their side score, but it was a stunner when it came.
